did_you_know.text: Did you know that the name 'El Shaddai,' by which God appeared to the patriarchs, is often translated as 'God Almighty' or 'God All-Sufficient'? It emphasizes God's ability to provide and protect.

Did you know that when God states His name 'YHWH' was not known to the patriarchs, it means they hadn't experienced Him as the fulfiller of His salvation promises in their entirety, as the Israelites would during the Exodus?

Did you know that in this verse, God makes four promises to Israel: 'I will bring you out,' 'I will rescue you,' 'I will redeem you,' and 'I will take you'? These are the traditional 'Four Expressions of Redemption' upon which the Four Cups of Wine at the Passover Seder are based.

Did you know that the phrase 'with an outstretched arm' depicts a powerful image of a long, strong arm extended to act decisively and with great force? It symbolizes God's miraculous and direct intervention in nature and history.

Did you know that when God says 'I swore to give' (literally, 'I lifted My hand'), it refers to taking an oath? Lifting one's hand was a common gesture for making a vow in the ancient world, signifying the seriousness and weight of the promise.

Did you know that the phrase 'because of their shortness of spirit' describes a state of such deep despair and mental exhaustion that the Israelites were unable to receive hope or hear the message of redemption?

Did you know that the phrase 'uncircumcised lips,' used by Moses to describe himself, is an idiom for having difficulty speaking, a lack of fluency, or inability to articulate clearly, similar to other expressions Moses used for his speech impediment?

Did you know that the three sons of Levi mentioned here – Gershon, Kohath, and Merari – later became the three main families of the Levites in the wilderness, each with specific duties in carrying and dismantling the Tabernacle?

Did you know that Amram's marriage to Jochebed, his aunt (his father's sister), was permissible in the period before the giving of the Torah? Such marriages were only later forbidden by the Mosaic Law (Leviticus 18).

Did you know that Elisheva, Aaron's wife, was the sister of Nahshon ben Amminadab from the tribe of Judah? Nahshon was known as one of the important leaders of the tribe of Judah, and later in history, the monarchy would emerge from his tribe.
